item.title: The Climates of Other Worlds: A Review of the Emerging Field of Exoplanet Climatology
Geostrophic wind induced by latitudinal variation in gravitational acceleration on oblate planets

notes: Welcome to our tour on terraforming, inspired by the world-building in Red Mars. We start by defining how we might deliberately reshape a planet's atmosphere and temperature to make it habitable.
Building on that goal, we look outward to other worlds. Recent discoveries show us many exoplanets, but harsh factors often prevent them from supporting life despite being in the right zone.

Stepping up a level, we examine how gravity and shape affect these distant planets. Tidal forces can lock a planet's rotation, creating unique wind patterns that differ greatly from what we see on Earth.
